title: The Impossible Orchard
premise: Marine biologist Wren Vasquez returns to her family's coastal orchard for a reunion she dreads, armed with a fake date: Elias Thorne, the quiet boat mechanic who once fixed her research vessel and never forgot her. What begins as a shield against her mother's matchmaking becomes real by dessert, but Wren's dream fellowship in Palau demands she leave within weeks — the same week the orchard's bankruptcy auction will tear her family apart. When a storm forces Wren to choose between a career-saving expedition and helping Elias save the grove, she discovers that survival was never just about staying afloat; it's about what you refuse to let sink. In the end, Wren declines the fellowship, Elias signs on as her research partner aboard a grant-funded coastal program, and they plant a new orchard row together — love, this time, with better timing.
about_author: Odile Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former tide-pool docent who writes romances set where salt air meets stubborn soil. She lives in a drafty farmhouse with an orchard of questionable productivity and a dog named Buoy.

chapters.title: Salt on the Rootstock
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren arrives at the Vasquez family orchard for the reunion, turtle-counting spreadsheets in hand as emotional armor, and impulsively recruits Elias — the boat mechanic she barely knows — to pose as her boyfriend. The chapter establishes her guilt over abandoning the family business and her fear that wanting things leads to losing them. Emotional beat: guarded deflection masking old grief over her father's death.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, mostly Wren. The fake date works too well: shared stories at dinner, a stolen almost-kiss under the avocado trees, and Elias quietly defending Wren when her brother accuses her of running away. But Wren learns the orchard faces auction in three weeks — and receives word her Palau fellowship departs the same week. Emotional beat: warmth curdling into panic as two futures collide.

chapters.title: The Storm We Chose
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A hurricane strikes the coast mid-auction-preparations; Elias and Wren spend the night securing the grove and sheltering neighbors, and he confesses he's loved her since the day she docked her battered research boat. At dawn, the fellowship calls: the expedition moved up, departure tomorrow. Wren, terrified of repeating her father's sacrifice, says yes. Emotional beat: climax — love declared, then seemingly lost to duty.

chapters.title: What Refuses to Sink
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the tarmac, Wren realizes the fellowship saved her once but cannot be her whole life now. She withdraws, then fights for both futures: proposing a grant-funded coastal conservation program based at the orchard, with Elias as partner. Her family votes to keep the land; the last scene shows them planting a new row of trees, hands in the same dirt. Emotional beat: resolution — second chances earned, not given.
